subject: Private upgrade contingency lattice & cutover traffic plan
messages:
From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai; marta.lopez@acmebio.com
Cc: ops@acmebio.com, vendor-netops@edgefabric.io
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private upgrade contingency lattice & cutover traffic plan

Team / Marta —

Posting the proposal for Acme's Private cluster maintenance next month. Goal: a short, low-risk upgrade window that lets Acme apply our runtime + kernel patch while preserving in-region SLAs and giving a clear, fast rollback path. Highlights in the attached spreadsheet: a three-tier "contingency lattice" that combines network containment, version pinning, and service-level circuit breakers.

Key asks:
- Ops to confirm the BGP quiesce and VIP failover window (we're proposing 01:00–03:00 UTC on Nov 6).
- Netops to validate the HAProxy ACLs and wireguard tunnel swap plan for traffic containment.
- Acme to confirm whether the customer-side proxy will accept fast DNS TTL flip during the canary.

Attached: upgrade-contingency-lattice.xlsx, net-diagram-zoneB-v2.png, maintenance-playbook-acme-v1.3.pdf

Short summary of the lattice tiers (in case someone opens email on mobile):
1) Contain — edge ACLs + connection draining at the ingress to prevent new sessions to patched nodes.
2) Canary + pin — 10% canary (control-plane pin for model-serving and runtime), KV cache warmup, confirm metrics.
3) Escalate (if canary bad) — immediate rollback to pinned version + VIP reroute to warm standby region.

Irene / Karthik, can you confirm the mechanism for forced KV cache flush without losing request affinity?
Naomi, please call out required runbook owners and the minimum telemetry to greenlight canary.

Marta / Acme — any constraints on the 01:00–03:00 UTC window? We can shift earlier/later but need a 3-hour contiguous window for the safety checks.

Connor
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: upgrade-contingency-lattice.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)]
[Attachment: net-diagram-zoneB-v2.png (image/png)]
[Attachment: maintenance-playbook-acme-v1.3.pdf (application/pdf)]

From: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai; marta.lopez@acmebio.com
Cc: ops@acmebio.com
Date: Tue, 20 Oct 2026 10:38:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private upgrade contingency lattice & cutover traffic plan

Thanks Connor — good framing. Quick notes from an ops/runbook perspective:

- KV cache — we should avoid a global flush. Recommend per-pod cache eviction coordinated with session-aware draining. Karthik, can you add the exact kubectl/drain + curl probes we should run? I sketched commands in the spreadsheet (tab: playbook-snippets).
- Traffic containment — instead of DNS TTL flip (which may be slow for some corporate proxies), prefer an ACL + HAProxy backend weight swap with immediate 503 gating for affected nodes. We already have that flow in NETOPS-4721.
- Rollback speed — add a pre-built pinned-image tag and an automation hook in the deploy pipeline so we can revert with a single "deploy --pin tag=acme-20261006-stable". That reduces human error.

I've attached an edited schedule with alternate windows (2300–0100 UTC and 03:00–05:00 UTC) and a shortened canary checklist. Also included the minimal telemetry set: 95th latency per route, error-rate by pod, kv-hit ratio, and http2 stream resets.

Naomi
Sr. SRE, Redwood Inference
[Attachment: upgrade-contingency-lattice.xlsx (revised - contains playbook-snippets)]

From: marta.lopez@acmebio.com
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Cc: ops@acmebio.com
Date: Wed, 21 Oct 2026 01:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private upgrade contingency lattice & cutover traffic plan

Connor / Naomi — thanks for the detailed plan. A few items from Acme side:

1) Window: 03:00–05:00 UTC on Nov 6 is preferable for us (less business traffic overnight).
2) DNS: we cannot rely on DNS TTL flips — our corporate proxy caches aggressively and may not clear in time. We request the HAProxy weight-swap approach and the VIP failover instead.
3) Standby region: we have a warm standby we can promote for at most 45 minutes. If rollback is needed beyond that, we will need an extended failover playbook which I can share.

Also: Our compliance team asked for an audit artifact that shows time-stamped operator actions for the rollback step (to be attached to SOC2 evidence). Can you include a DocuSign approval or an ops run-book signoff entry?

I'll loop in our sysnet lead if we get to the failover cutover stage.

Marta
IT Ops Lead
Acme Biotech

From: karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
To: connor_obrien@redwood.ai, naomi_feldman@redwood.ai
Cc: marta.lopez@acmebio.com, irene_choi@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 22 Oct 2026 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private upgrade contingency lattice & cutover traffic plan

Acknowledged. A couple of technical clarifications and actions from my side:

- KV eviction: will implement per-pod cache eviction using a preStop hook that triggers an atomic key migration to the warm standby. Command snippet: kubectl rollout restart --namespace=private --selector=app=redwood-runtime && curl -sS http://localhost:9090/healthz?wait=10 to validate warmup. Full snippet in the sheet.
- HAProxy flow: I will push the ACL snippet to NETOPS-4721 and request EdgeFabric to simulate the 50/50 weight-swap in their staging. If successful, we promote to 90/10 then 0/100 within the 30m canary.
- Operator audit: we'll add an automated runbook step that posts a signed entry to the Acme audit S3 (pre-shared bucket) and return a signed URL to include in compliance artifacts. DocuSign link can be attached to the signoff process.

I'll run a dry-run simulation in our staging the week of Oct 26 and post results to the Drive link.

Karthik
Staff Engineer, Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: connor_obrien@redwood.ai
To: naomi_feldman@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai, irene_choi@redwood.ai; marta.lopez@acmebio.com, ops@acmebio.com
Date: Fri, 23 Oct 2026 11:48:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private upgrade contingency lattice & cutover traffic plan

Thanks everyone — plan updated and locked to 03:00–05:00 UTC on 2026-11-06 per Acme request. Next steps: 

1) Karthik runs the staging dry-run (Oct 26) and posts log + canary metrics to the Drive folder.
2) Naomi to own the runbook owners list and on-call rotation for the window.
3) Acme to confirm the pre-shared S3 bucket permissions so we can write the operator audit artifact.
4) I will send a DocuSign signoff for the maintenance authorization tomorrow; please sign so ops can commence at T-24.

Deliverables added to the Drive folder and JIRA NETOPS-4721 updated with owners. I'll allocate a 1h shiproom at T-2 to triage any last-minute blockers.

Connor
Director, Platform Operations
Redwood Inference
